name: How They Survived
niche: Curiosity history: how ordinary people actually survived and solved everyday problems before modern life (winter without heating, food without fridges, medicine, travel, cities). Promise: the clever, surprising, very human engineering of daily life in the past.
audience: Men and women 25-65, curious, like survival, old skills, how-things-worked and history without dry dates. Proven by small new channels getting millions of views: Past Trek, Fossil, Relic Explains, StickOrbit.
format: One burning question ('how did people...?'). Open with a vivid life-or-death situation -> 5-7 real solutions or eras, each with a mini-story, how it physically worked (explain the mechanism so the viewer could rebuild it), what it cost, a twist -> what we forgot. Maps, timelines, cutaway logic. Never dry lists of dates.
honesty: Only verifiable history and physics. Numbers need a real source; disputed claims get ONE honest hedge. Never invent quotes or statistics. Avoid human-evolution claims (say 'hunters of the Ice Age', not 'early humans evolved'), avoid glorifying idols, pagan rituals, magic or superstition; if a past belief matters mention it briefly and neutrally as what people did, without endorsing. No nudity, no sexual topics, no gore beyond a factual mention.
character_w: a young woman in a long brown cloak and a plain headscarf
notes: New channel 2026-10-31. Best competitor frames: 'How Long You'd Last in Every X' (12M), 'How Ancient Inuit Slept Safely...' (1.1M, 3k subs), 'How Did Mountain Men Sleep Through Freezing Nights' (389k).
